subject: twins
one_liner: A browser IDE for twins. Every keystroke is attributed to the correct twin, or to the older one if we can't tell.
brand_voice_notes: Fork talks like a developer-tools company that has quietly become a family court. It is calm, exact, and treats sibling liability as a core infrastructure problem. Confidence percentages are always specific and always low. Birth order is cited the way other companies cite SOC 2. Never cute about twins, never says 'double the fun'. Every joke is a policy.

hero.h1: Two developers. One face. No plausible deniability.
hero.sub: Fork is a cloud IDE built for twins. Every line of code is signed, timestamped and attributed to the correct sibling with 61% confidence.

features.title: Blame Arbitration
features.blurb: git blame was built for strangers. Ours weighs keystroke cadence, chair height and birth order, then names a twin. When the model ties, the older twin is liable. This is in the terms.

features.title: Telepathic Merge
features.blurb: Conflicting edits are resolved by assuming you both meant the same thing. If you didn't, one of you will by Thursday.

features.title: Mirror Mode
features.blurb: Your cursor and your sibling's cursor move in lockstep across a vertical seam. Output is unchanged. The screen recordings are excellent.

demo_screen_concept: A Fork workspace shared by twins Priya and Pooja Raman. Left: a file tree for a repo called 'shipment-router'. Centre: a code editor showing a Python file where every line has a gutter stripe in vermilion (Pooja) or cobalt (Priya), with a per-line authorship confidence. Right: a Blame Arbitration panel listing disputed lines with evidence (keystroke cadence, chair height, who was holding the coffee) and a 'Dispute' button that opens an evidence modal where you can file an appeal. A 'Birth-order liability' toggle reassigns every tied line to the older twin and recounts the totals. A presence bar shows both twins with photo avatars. A Run button executes the tests, one fails, and the console prints a liability assignment.

design_direction.style: Merge-conflict diff viewer with bilateral symmetry, paper daylight mode. The page is staged as a side-by-side code review of two people who share a face. Everything comes in pairs split by a vertical seam: left is Twin A (vermilion), right is Twin B (cobalt). Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: infrared, data strips, viewfinder brackets, contours, thumbnail circles and arrows, highlighter swipes, VHS labels, OSD menus, tracking lines, 24-hour bars, Swiss poster grids, giant numerals, candlelight, foil rules, menu leaders, ruled worksheets, stickers, red pen, large-print sliders. Also absent: dark mode, glassmorphism, neon, gradients behind body text. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The conflict marker: section dividers are git conflict markers set in mono (<<<<<<< twin/a, =======, >>>>>>> twin/b), the left one vermilion, the right cobalt. (2) The gutter stripe: cards and quotes carry a 4px left stripe in the twin colour that 'wrote' them, plus a small mono line number. (3) The seam: a 1px dashed ink line runs down the hero's vertical centre, and the h1 is echoed on the right as a faint mirrored ghost. (4) The two cursors: blinking 2px text cursors in vermilion and cobalt, each with a tiny name flag, sit in the hero headline and the pricing header. Corners are 4px. Shadows are a single 1px ink hairline, never blur. Headings are Space Grotesk 700, sentence case, -0.03em. Body is IBM Plex Sans 17px/1.62. Every figure, line number, confidence and price is IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures.

design_direction.archetype: Developer-tools SaaS landing (cloud IDE): announcement bar, nav, centred type hero with a product editor mock, three bordered feature tiles, testimonials, three-tier pricing table, footer.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Two cursors blink out of phase (530ms, offset 265ms). On load the hero editor mock types two lines, one per twin, alternating. Conflict markers slide their halves in from opposite sides on scroll (transform only, 240ms ease-out), gated on a .js class with a timeout fallback. Everything respects prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Centred h1 with the vermilion and cobalt cursors parked inside it, the subhead and a single solid ink CTA beneath. Below, a wide editor mock split down the middle by the dashed seam: left pane authored by Twin A, right pane by Twin B, the same function written twice with one character different, and a small 'Blame Arbitration: 61% Twin A' chip straddling the seam.
